newsitem.title: UK: UK Economist Group appoints new chief exec..
newsitem.headline: UK Economist Group appoints new chief exec..

text.p: British media giant Pearson Plc's Economist Group said on Tuesday it had appointed Helen Alexander as the publishing firm's new chief executive to replace Marjorie Scardino who was recently made chief executive of Pearson.

Alexander, who gives up her post as managing director of the group's information division -- the Economist Intelligence Unit -- will take over as company head from January 1, 1997, an Economist spokeswoman told Reuters.

The move is part of a top-level reshuffle initiated nearly two weeks ago with the appointment of Scardino -- who replaces outgoing chief executive Frank Barlow at the end of the year -- and Dennis Stevenson as Pearson's new chairman.
Pearson, publisher of the Financial Times British business daily, owns half of the Economist Group.
The Economist turned in profits after tax of 17.7 million stg this year from 7.8 million in 1993.

Pearson shares, which suffered an attack of jitters on the announcement of the management changes on October 17, have since recovered to near year-high levels. At 1157 GMT the shares stood at 740 pence, up two pence on yesterday's close.
